newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel's Netanyahu seeks to revive growth in 1998.
newsitem.headline: Israel's Netanyahu seeks to revive growth in 1998.

text.p: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu delayed discussion of next year's budget on Sunday, saying the Treasury must submit proposals to revive economic growth in 1998.
Last week the Treasury announced it expected growth of only 3.0 to 3.5 percent in 1998, following a rise in gross domestic product (GDP) of only 2.5 percent in 1997.
For most of this decade Israel has enjoyed annual growth of six percent or more.
The Treasury presented its economic forecast to Netanyahu on Friday and was to submit it to the cabinet on Sunday, marking the start of discussion of the 1998 budget.
Instead, Netanyahu put off discussion on the 1998 outlook until August 10 and asked the Treasury to submit to the cabinet on the same data proposals to revive economic growth next year.
Treasury officials said Netanyahu rejected the Treasury's forecast as too pessimistic.
Netanyahu and Finance Minister Yaacov Neeman downplayed talk of a dispute between the two.
The prime minister's office issued a statement saying that Netanyahu and Neeman agreed to discuss the two issues jointly.

"I am sure the ministers know that the different forecasts, with which I have no argument, say that if we take a certain path we will be in a year of continued economic slowdown also in 1998," Netanyahu's office quoted the prime minister as saying during Sunday's cabinet meeting.

"I said that we must, first of all, discuss things that will bring growth. Today...we could discuss one forecast or another but it seems to me that our job around the government's table is not to deal with analytical forecasts of what will be if we don't take certain steps but rather the main question is what we must do so that the forecast will change."
Netanyahu said the government must at the start adopt a target of growth.

Finance Minister Yaacov Neeman also maintained there was no row. "That decision was taken at my initiative," he said in reference to the plan to discuss the 1998 forecast and proposals for growth together on August 10.
Treasury officials said implementation of structural reform in the economy could improve the forecast.
The Treasury's forecast called for GDP per capita to rise by a slight 0.8 to 1.3 percent in 1998 against an estimated increase of 0.2 percent this year.
Unemployment is expected to reach 7.9 percent in 1998 from 7.7 percent this year.
The cabinet will hold a meeting in the first week of September to set the budget for the individual ministries, the statement from the prime minister's office said.
